tvs.title-bl-seo: Why do your brows every day when you can have microblading?
tvs.text-bl-seo: You might think that using makeup every day is a much quicker and cheaper solution. But if you add up how much money, time and effort goes into daily makeup over the 1.5–2 years that microblading lasts, you will realize that an eyebrow tattoo is far more convenient in every respect. Imagine waking up in the morning and no longer having to fill in your brows and try to shape them. You won’t need to check them in the mirror throughout the day. With affordable eyebrow micropigmentation, you can always be sure your brows look exactly the way you want: groomed and gorgeous. You won’t even need to tint or brush them. They will look perfect!

tvs.title_bl1_about: Microblading for femininity and natural beauty
tvs.text_bl1_about: Eyebrow microblading is considered one of the best-known techniques. And no wonder, since this micropigmentation can solve a number of key concerns related to both your appearance and your natural beauty. With microblading, brows become wider, thicker, longer, fuller and more defined. An eyebrow tattoo can partially reshape the brows where hairs have fallen out, or recreate them completely from scratch if, for whatever reason, the hairs are missing. Eyebrow micropigmentation will also camouflage scars, acne marks, freckles and other flaws that bother you. And all of this in an hour and a half! You won’t feel any discomfort either: microblading is painless thanks to the anesthetic and the professionalism of the artists at our LBar studio. So put away the makeup, simplify your life and choose an eyebrow tattoo.

tvs.title-bl-faq: Answers to frequently asked questions about microblading
tvs.text-bl-seo-2:
Microblading benefits

Beyond the aesthetic appeal, eyebrow micropigmentation solves a number of problems. First of all, it may be the best option if your natural brows are sparse, have partly fallen out or are missing altogether. In this case, microblading can visually create brows with the length, width, density and color tailored to you. The technique can also be an excellent choice if you:

  • need to cover imperfections in the brow area, such as scars, pigmentation spots or freckles. Microblading lets you visually hide all of these flaws;
  • need to correct the shape or thickness of your brows. In this case, the tattoo will visually hide asymmetry and make the brows thicker, longer, darker or more vivid;
  • want to feel comfortable. Brows play an important role in your appearance, so they should always be in perfect shape. Beautiful, well-groomed brows make the whole face look well-groomed too. They also boost your self-confidence.

Features of the microblading technique

There are two microblading techniques for drawing in brows: Eastern and European. The European technique is used less often and looks less natural, because all the hairs are drawn with the same length, thickness, color and direction. Artists most often recommend it when only part of the brow needs to be drawn in. The Eastern technique, on the other hand, is more accessible and more widely used, because the hairs are drawn to fully imitate natural hair, with varying thickness, length, direction and even shade. With this technique, brows that are missing can be created from scratch and brought as close as possible to a natural look. It is worth noting that no matter how skilled and experienced the artist is, microblading cannot create completely natural brows. Visually, it will be clear that the hairs are not real. There will also be visible gaps between the strokes, showing that they are artificial. In such cases, artists often combine two techniques: microblading and the powder effect. The first creates the “structure”, while the second adds a tinted base layer that fills in those gaps. As a result, the brows look harmonious and as natural as possible. Microblading does not cover an old tattoo. The old tattoo will remain fully visible, however dense the hair strokes are. This is due to the difference in shade between the old tattoo and the new micropigmentation, as well as the spaces between the strokes, which leave small gaps.

Contraindications

Microblading has a number of contraindications. The most obvious include diabetes (type 1 and type 2), epilepsy, skin conditions and inflammation, pregnancy and breastfeeding. Microblading can be done during your period. It is important to be in good health for the procedure. If you are feeling unwell, it is best to reschedule for another day.

Preparing for microblading and aftercare

Avoid excessive alcohol and caffeine before the procedure. Ideally, don’t drink any coffee at all that day. Avoid taking anticoagulants the day before your session. Where possible, it is also advisable to pause hormonal medication for a while. Don’t wear any brow makeup when you come in for the procedure.
It is important to pay special attention to your skin after microblading. This technique is a specific procedure that involves injuring the skin with a fine blade, and the skin needs care in order to heal. Right after the session, your artist should recommend products to help the skin heal and recover. Just in case, keep chlorhexidine on hand to disinfect the skin and remove any lymph fluid that seeps out.

Stages of the microblading procedure

The microblading procedure begins with drawing a sketch. The artist will follow it exactly while creating your makeup. The sketch also lets you see in advance how your brows will look after micropigmentation. Once the sketch is approved, the artist applies an anesthetic. It takes about 15–20 minutes to take effect, and then the artist gets to work. During the procedure, an additional anesthetic is applied to reduce pain, redness and possible skin inflammation. At the end of the session, the artist will give you aftercare advice and book your touch-up appointment.
A touch-up is essential with microblading. As the skin regenerates, some of the pigment is shed and the hair strokes become lighter. The touch-up restores the strokes’ intensity and can also adjust their shade, length or thickness. It is best done as soon as the skin has healed and recovered, usually one month after your first visit to the studio.

Microblading is highly valued by women for good reason. One short procedure transforms the whole look of the face. And when a woman feels beautiful and confident, every day is a true joy.

migx_questions.questions-title: What makes the microblading technique different?
migx_questions.questions-text: Microblading differs significantly from other permanent makeup techniques. Instead of a tattoo machine, the procedure uses a manual tool – a small pen fitted with a microblade that makes fine, hair-like incisions in the skin. Pigment is then introduced into these incisions. The result is brows with ideal volume, color and density.
No. The procedure is painless thanks to an anesthetic, which is used both before and during the procedure. You don’t need to worry about pain – we guarantee you won’t feel any.

migx_questions.questions-title: How long does eyebrow micropigmentation last?
migx_questions.questions-text: It depends on your skin type and age – on average, 1.5–2 years. Microblading is not recommended for women with oily skin, because of the risk of the pigment blurring when it mixes with the skin’s oils.

migx_questions.questions-title: Can I have microblading during pregnancy?
migx_questions.questions-text: The procedure is contraindicated for pregnant and breastfeeding women.
